documents.description: Declarations this capability SHIPS and the interpreter reads: a name, a payload file, and the schema that judges it. The base declaration stays thin -- a capability that needs a lifecycle brings its own document and its own schema rather than growing a field on every other capability.

governs.description: This capability holds a collection of things that move through a declared lifecycle. Every name here points at something declared elsewhere in THIS file -- never at a path, because the path is already declared by the install that owns it.

composes.description: This capability holds things that are COMPOSED rather than authored: a BASE stating what is true of a kind, an INSTANCE stating what is true of one of them, and a definition that is the projection of the two. Every name here points at something declared elsewhere in THIS file. What the block is FOR is what it makes unreachable: the base is declared once and rendered into every definition, so a binding line is not a line anyone is trusted to keep in step -- it is a line nobody can restate. An instance never overrides; a key carried by both sides is refused, because precedence is how the loser's declaration goes on reading as true while the value came from somewhere else.

sources.description: The named documents holding bases -- SHIPPED by this capability, or AUTHORED by the host in a path it declared readable. Both arrive by name and neither outranks the other: a base a host declares is a base, which is what lets a thing with no shipped ancestor be the same grammar rather than an exception to it.

named_by.description: The field on an instance that names its base.

shared.description: Lines carried by EVERY definition whatever its base -- declared once, rendered into all. This is the half a reference could not do, because a reference can be left unfollowed.

census.description: The view-model name for the roll of BASES with the instances each one has -- including the ones with none. A base shipped and never taken up is a fact; a surface that merely omitted it would read exactly like a kit that never shipped it.

evaluates.description: This capability holds things that are JUDGED: a declaration the host owns, naming what is judged and how, and a collection of judgements over it. Every name here points at something declared elsewhere in THIS file, or at a field of the document it names -- never at a path, and never at a case, a rubric or a verdict, because those are the host's and the framework has no way to know a good one. The verb that reads this block opens a judgement for every pair that lacks one and writes no verdict at all.

observes.description: This capability declares that something WATCHES a run: which kind of observer, and the runs it applies to. An observer is opened before the verb and closed after it, so a run that never comes back has already said that it started. WHICH runs are worth watching is stated here, as data, never decided in the machinery -- a rule about a host's runs spelled in an interpreter is a judgement in the one place a host cannot reach.

when.description: The fields of the run's own reading this row reads, and the values it reads them as. Equality only: the instant a declaration can express a comparison it can express a policy, and a policy inside a declaration is a thing no machine may generate and no host may safely edit.

reads_as.description: This installed path is READ BACK under this name, and reaches every projection. A target ending in '/' is a collection of JSON files; anything else is one document. The path is stated once, here, by the install that owns it.

each.description: This projection writes one file PER RECORD rather than one file about a set. Required exactly when the declared target names a collection -- the same '/' rule that decides whether a readable is one document or many, read once and never a second convention. A surface FOR each member, where the singular form gives a surface ABOUT them all.
